newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben chief editor Berger leaves.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben chief editor Berger leaves.

text.p: Recently-floated German television group ProSieben Media AG said on Friday chief editor Gerd Berger was leaving the company, and it would reduce the amount of in-house productions aired on its channels.
ProSieben, which runs the ProSieben and Kabel 1 cable TV channels, said Jan Koerbelin would take responsibility for all output. Berger will not be replaced, a spokesman said.
ProSieben said it wanted to reduce its number of in-house television productions towards the end of 1998, and instead contract out more programme making to independent production companies.
"We will invest more money in programmes and less in bureaucracy," chief executive Georg Kofler said in a statement, adding ProSieben shareholders would benefit.
ProSieben attracted huge interest in its initial public offering earlier this month -- the first by a German television company. The issue was 50 times oversubscribed.
Its preferred shares, issued at 72 marks, traded as high as 98 marks but have since fallen back. The stock eased in bourse trading on Friday to close at 85.05 marks, down 2.95 marks.
